blocks.html: To send bulk WhatsApp messages in India without getting blocked, use the official WhatsApp Business API with approved templates, message only customers who opted in, and send content relevant enough that people do not block you. Blasting a list from a normal number or an unofficial tool is the fastest way to lose that number, and often the customers behind it.

This guide explains why WhatsApp blocks bulk senders, the safe official route, how opt-in and templates work, the limits that stop some messages from delivering, and a checklist for your first campaign, for marketers, D2C brands and SMBs across India. sections.heading: How to Send Bulk WhatsApp Messages Without Getting Blocked: The Short Answer

sections.heading: Opt-In: The Rule That Protects Your Number

blocks.html: Opt-in is the single most important rule. Meta's WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy says you may contact only people who gave you their number and agreed to receive messages from you.

items.title: A clear yes:
items.desc: the customer actively agrees. Pre-ticked boxes and bundled terms are weak consent.

items.title: Your business name:
items.desc: state who will be messaging them.

items.title: The message types:
items.desc: say what they will receive, for example order updates or offers.

items.title: Before the first message:
items.desc: collect it first, outside WhatsApp, such as on your website, at checkout, by SMS, by phone or in store.

items.title: An easy way out:
items.desc: tell people they can opt out at any time, and honour it.

blocks.html: Displaying your WhatsApp number does not count as opt-in. A safe checkbox reads: "Send me order updates and offers from [Business name] on WhatsApp." Meta is also rolling out a setting that lets users control marketing messages from businesses, including opting out and marking offers as interested or not interested. Treat consent under the DPDP Act the same way: a clear purpose, easy withdrawal, and records you can show.

sections.heading: Templates and Categories: Getting Approved the First Time

blocks.html: To message customers first, you need approved templates. The category you choose decides the rules and how Meta bills you, and a wrong category is a common reason for rejection.

items.title: Marketing:
items.desc: offers, launches, reminders to buy and win-backs. Send these only to opted-in customers.

items.title: Utility:
items.desc: transactional messages tied to something the customer did, such as order and payment updates.

items.title: Authentication:
items.desc: OTPs and verification codes. See WhatsApp OTP vs SMS OTP.

items.title: Write for one purpose:
items.desc: one clear message, one clear button, and your business name so customers recognise you.

items.title: Watch template feedback:
items.desc: a template can move from active to paused or disabled when customers react badly to it.

sections.heading: Messaging Limits and Frequency Caps: Why Some Messages Do Not Deliver

blocks.html: Even with perfect consent, two limits can stop a message. They are separate, and neither means your number is in trouble.

items.title: Your messaging limit:
items.desc: the number of unique users you can start conversations with in a rolling 24 hours outside a customer service window. It starts low and grows as you send quality messages. Check your current limit in WhatsApp Manager.

items.title: Meta's per-user marketing cap:
items.desc: Meta can limit how many marketing templates one person receives from all businesses combined. Meta does not publish a fixed number.

items.title: Error 131049:
items.desc: a marketing template was not delivered because the recipient reached that cap. Meta advises waiting at least 24 hours before retrying that user.

items.title: What to do:
items.desc: pace your sends, prioritise your most engaged customers, and do not retry the same user repeatedly.

sections.heading: WhatsApp, SMS and DLT: What Applies to Which Channel

blocks.html: DLT registration is a TRAI requirement for SMS only. WhatsApp follows Meta's template approval and opt-in policies. If you add an SMS fallback for customers who cannot receive WhatsApp, that SMS still needs your DLT entity, sender ID and approved template. See our guide to DLT registration charges in India, and read how the same idea works on RCS in RCS messaging for e-commerce.

Meta bills per delivered template message, based on the category and the recipient's country, and marketing templates have their own rate. We do not quote rates here, because Meta revises them and your invoice must match the current rate card. Check Meta's official pricing page before you plan a campaign, and ask any provider for an itemised quote that separates Meta's charges from platform fees and any SMS fallback. items.q: Can I send bulk WhatsApp messages from my normal WhatsApp or the Business app?
items.a: Not safely. WhatsApp's own FAQ says its products are not intended for bulk or automated messaging, and that doing so violates its Terms of Service. Using unofficial tools, browser extensions or modified apps for this can get your number restricted or banned. For bulk sending, use the WhatsApp Business Platform through a provider.

items.q: Why does WhatsApp block or ban numbers for bulk messaging?
items.a: The usual causes are using the apps or unofficial tools for bulk or automated sending, messaging people who never opted in, and sending messages recipients block or report. WhatsApp and Meta monitor how recipients react, and templates or numbers with poor feedback can be paused, restricted or disabled.

items.q: How do I send bulk WhatsApp messages safely in India?
items.a: Use the WhatsApp Business API through a provider, collect clear opt-in before the first message, send only approved templates in the right category, segment your audience, keep a visible opt-out, and start with small batches while you watch delivery and block signals. Keep SMS as a fallback for customers who cannot receive WhatsApp.

items.q: Do I need opt-in to send bulk WhatsApp messages?
items.a: Yes. Meta's WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy says you may contact only people who gave you their number and agreed to receive messages from you. The opt-in should name your business and the types of messages, be collected before you send, and tell people they can opt out. Displaying your own WhatsApp number does not count as opt-in.

items.q: Is bulk WhatsApp messaging legal in India?
items.a: Sending through the official WhatsApp Business Platform to customers who consented is permitted by WhatsApp's policy. You must still follow Indian law, including the DPDP Act's principles of clear consent, a stated purpose and easy withdrawal. This is practical guidance rather than legal advice, so check your obligations with a qualified professional.

items.q: Does bulk WhatsApp messaging need DLT registration?
items.a: No. DLT registration under TRAI's rules applies to SMS. WhatsApp messages follow Meta's template approval and opt-in policies instead. If you add an SMS fallback, that SMS channel still needs your DLT entity, sender ID and approved template.

items.q: Why are some of my WhatsApp marketing messages not delivered?
items.a: Two limits can apply. Your messaging limit caps how many unique users you can start conversations with in a rolling 24 hours. Separately, Meta can limit how many marketing templates one person receives from all businesses combined, and Meta advises waiting at least 24 hours before retrying that user. Neither means your number is unhealthy.

items.q: What should I do if my WhatsApp number is restricted?
items.a: Stop sending, and review how you collected opt-in, which templates you used and whether any unofficial tool touched the number. Fix the cause before you resume, and follow the appeal steps shown in your WhatsApp or Meta account. Ask your provider to check your quality signals, and avoid retrying the same campaign immediately.
